messages.updates.title: Updates
messages.updates.subtitle: Manage DiskSnoop versions, release notes, and updates.
messages.updates.availableText: A newer version is available. Automatic download can prepare the update without restarting the app.
messages.updates.downloadedText: The file was downloaded. Because this is the portable channel, open the installer/file manually.
messages.updates.restartText: The installer downloaded the update. DiskSnoop only restarts when you confirm.
messages.updates.defaultText: The app can check for new versions without interrupting your work.
messages.updates.assistedText: On the portable build, DiskSnoop checks and downloads the new version, but it does not replace the running executable. Use the downloaded file or the releases page to update manually.
messages.updates.autoText: On the installed channel, DiskSnoop downloads the update automatically and only restarts to apply it after your confirmation.
messages.updates.restartUnavailablePortable: Automatic restart is unavailable in portable
messages.updates.diagnosticsText: Use this block to confirm the published release matches the app type currently running.

messages.updates.betaNote: The Beta channel is enabled in preferences. Disable this option to search only stable releases.
messages.updates.localChangelog: Showing local notes for the installed version. When a published release includes a changelog, it appears here automatically.
messages.updates.noChangelog: No changelog is available yet. If a release is published, you can still open the releases page to review it manually.
messages.updates.prefManual: Use manual update even in the installer

messages.doubt.intro: I found this item in a disk scanner (DiskSnoop):
messages.doubt.question: Is it safe to delete this item, or should I review it manually first?
messages.doubt.batchIntro: I found these candidates in a disk scanner (DiskSnoop):
messages.doubt.batchQuestion: Analyze each item separately and indicate whether it is probably safe to delete, should be reviewed, or should be kept. Briefly explain why.
messages.doubt.batchResponseFormat:
At the end, return one line per item using exactly one of these formats:
<ID> | APAGAR
<ID> | MANTER
<ID> | REVISAR
You may include explanations before or after these lines.
messages.candidates.copyDoubtToast: Text copied. Paste it into an AI or search engine to investigate.
messages.candidates.copySelectedDoubtToast: Question for the selected items copied. Paste it into an AI to analyze them.
messages.candidates.aiImportHelp: Paste the AI response. DiskSnoop will read only lines in the format ID | APAGAR, ID | MANTER, or ID | REVISAR.
messages.candidates.aiImportPlaceholder: Paste the full AI response here...
messages.candidates.aiDeleteSelectionSummary: {selected} of {total} APAGAR items selected. {protected} are protected. No files were changed.

messages.history.timelineAria: Historical chart of reviewable size and logical size deleted by scan
messages.history.chartSubtitle: Logical sizes of eligible candidates and deleted items. Free-space changes are measured separately.
messages.cleanup.selectVisible: Select eligible candidates on this page
messages.cleanup.visible: {visible} of {total} candidates visible. The default filter shows low-risk items and items that need review.
messages.cleanup.rescanToMove: Run a new scan to verify this item's identity and safety before moving it.
messages.cleanup.action.low: Close the app or tool that uses this data and review the item before moving it to quarantine.
messages.cleanup.action.review: Open the location, confirm what the item is used for, and make sure you can recover it before moving it to quarantine.
messages.cleanup.action.high: Keep the item until you confirm its purpose and a way to recover it. DiskSnoop makes this finding available for manual review.
messages.cleanup.action.keep: Keep the item in place. Use the app or its package manager's maintenance tools to free space.
messages.cleanup.restriction.system: This path is in a protected area used by Windows or installed programs.
messages.cleanup.restriction.runtime: The path or directory structure indicates a runtime, virtual environment, or internal libraries.
messages.cleanup.restriction.application: The path or directory structure indicates an installed app, game, extension, or package.
messages.cleanup.restriction.protectedDescendant: This folder contains a protected item or content whose safety could not be verified.
messages.cleanup.restriction.linkedContent: Links, junctions, or files with multiple hard links were found. The app blocks moving this item as a whole.
messages.cleanup.restriction.unverified: Some content was excluded, could not be opened, or uses a special file type.
messages.cleanup.reason.internalDependency: The context points to an app or runtime dependency.
messages.cleanup.reason.nodeProject: The manifest beside node_modules points to dependencies of a Node.js project.
messages.cleanup.reason.projectOutput: The folder name and adjacent manifests suggest build output.
messages.cleanup.reason.npmCache: The path matches npm's package cache.
messages.cleanup.reason.npmRoot: The name points to npm's data directory. It can contain more than the package cache.
messages.cleanup.reason.offlineCache: The directory structure matches a service worker's CacheStorage.
messages.cleanup.reason.shaderCache: The location and name match a shader cache.
messages.cleanup.reason.mediaCache: The path matches a known media editing cache location.
messages.cleanup.reason.browserCache: The folder name and app profile are consistent with a Chromium or Electron cache.
messages.cleanup.reason.unknownCache: The name suggests a cache or temporary data. The purpose of the contents could not be verified.
messages.cleanup.reason.downloadFolder: The folder is in Downloads and the observed files meet the age threshold.
messages.cleanup.reason.downloadInstaller: The age, Downloads location, and installer name or package format point to a possible downloaded installer.
messages.cleanup.reason.archive: The format, age, and size indicate an old archive.
messages.cleanup.reason.log: The extension, age, and size indicate an old log file.
messages.cleanup.reason.temp: The extension and age point to a possible temporary file.
messages.cleanup.reason.unknownExecutableOrBackup: The format may represent an executable, disk image, or backup still in use. Its current purpose could not be verified.
messages.cleanup.reason.largeFile: The size exceeds the configured large-file threshold.
messages.cleanup.reason.downloadFile: The Downloads location, age, and size meet the detection thresholds.
messages.cleanup.impact.protected: Moving this folder or file could disrupt an app, runtime, or other dependent content.
messages.cleanup.impact.internalDependency: The app or environment could stop working after removal.
messages.cleanup.impact.nodeProject: The project may fail to build or start until its dependencies are reinstalled.
messages.cleanup.impact.projectOutput: You may need to rebuild the output. A published or manually edited copy may be unique.
messages.cleanup.impact.npmCache: npm may download packages again and offline installations may fail.
messages.cleanup.impact.npmRoot: npm may lose offline data or logs useful for diagnosis.
messages.cleanup.impact.offlineCache: The site may lose content stored for offline use until it downloads it again.
messages.cleanup.impact.shaderCache: Shaders may be rebuilt, temporarily slowing app startup or use.
messages.cleanup.impact.mediaCache: Previews and derived media may need to be regenerated.
messages.cleanup.impact.browserCache: The app may need to download and rebuild cached data.
messages.cleanup.impact.unknownCache: The folder may hold sessions, settings, dependencies, or unique content.
messages.cleanup.impact.downloadFolder: The folder may contain the only copy of downloaded or edited files.
messages.cleanup.impact.downloadInstaller: You may lose the copy needed to reinstall the program or use its installer offline.
messages.cleanup.impact.archive: The archive may be the only copy of the files it contains.
messages.cleanup.impact.log: Older diagnostic records may be lost.
messages.cleanup.impact.temp: The app may still need the file to complete or recover an operation.
messages.cleanup.impact.unknownExecutableOrBackup: Removal could stop a program from running or remove a recovery copy.
messages.cleanup.impact.largeFile: Size does not establish whether the file can be recovered or recreated.
messages.cleanup.impact.downloadFile: This may be the only copy, and the file may no longer be available to download.
messages.cleanup.evidence.profile: Profile markers in the parent folder
messages.cleanup.evidence.project: Project manifests in the parent folder
messages.cleanup.evidence.legacy: Evidence from an earlier report (location unrecorded)
messages.cleanup.modifiedTimeNote: This modification date is unusual and may have been set during packaging or extraction. It does not indicate when the item was last used.
messages.cleanup.restriction.installedDependency: This path contains or belongs to a package installed in node_modules.
messages.cleanup.restriction.packageManager: This path belongs to a managed package distribution, installation, or package store.
messages.cleanup.restriction.persistentProfile: This structure includes persistent profile data. The whole directory is protected.
messages.cleanup.reason.componentCache: The path points to the browser's component download cache.
messages.cleanup.impact.componentCache: The browser may need to download components again. Updates may be unavailable offline.
messages.cleanup.reason.editorCache: The path matches the editor's CachedData location. Version-named folders strengthen the evidence.
messages.cleanup.impact.editorCache: The editor may rebuild compiled data and take longer to start.
messages.cleanup.reason.electronDownloads: The path and hash-named subfolders are consistent with an Electron distribution download cache.
messages.cleanup.impact.electronDownloads: Installation may need to download the package again and can fail offline.
messages.cleanup.reason.cefProfile: The folder holds at least one CEF profile and may include persistent data.
messages.cleanup.impact.cefProfile: Moving the entire profile could affect sessions, history, or settings.
messages.cleanup.spaceNote: Totals use logical sizes. Moving items within the same volume keeps the files on that drive. Observed free space is shown in History.
messages.history.observedFreeDelta: Free-space change observed during the last scan: {value}
messages.cleanup.restriction.sharedDictionary: The cache and metadata database belong to the same Chromium dictionary store.
messages.cleanup.reason.sharedDictionaryCache: Dictionary data lives in this cache. Its metadata database is in the parent directory.
messages.cleanup.impact.sharedDictionaryCache: Moving only the data can leave references without content. Use the browser controls to clear dictionaries.
messages.cleanup.quarantineVisible: {count} items in quarantine or pending a move.
messages.cleanup.pendingMoveHelp: The move was interrupted or could not be verified as complete. Check both the original location and quarantine before taking action.
messages.cleanup.unverifiedOrigin: The original location of this item could not be verified. Open it in quarantine for manual review.
messages.cleanup.nativeDeleteMessage: Permanently delete this item from quarantine?
